-71.26380,42.39280.name: Boston IVF, LLC
-71.26380,42.39280.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Michael M. Alper, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-65.41197,-24.77232.name: Vitae Medicina Reproductiva
-65.41197,-24.77232.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

126.66432,45.76321.name: Harbin Veterinary Research Institute (HVRI)
126.66432,45.76321.state: China, Heilongjiang, Harbin, Nangang, 人和街 邮政编码: 150008, China
126.66432,45.76321.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences (CAAS). It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on animal health. Operational or announced: 1948. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

34.81000,31.90700.name: Weizmann Institute — stem-cell embryo models
34.81000,31.90700.desc: Grew structures from stem cells in 2023 that developed the features of a human embryo at fourteen days without egg, sperm or fertilisation. Every embryo research law in the world defines an embryo by fertilisation, so these fall outside all of them — including the fourteen-day limit that has governed the field since 1979.
